title: Connecting the Dots with Context Graphs — Stephen Chin, Neo4j
talk_summary: A Neo4j devrel talk pitching 'context graphs' (knowledge graphs + vector search + agent memory) as a way to ground agent decisions in connected enterprise data and store short-term, long-term, and reasoning memory. It is mostly conceptual and demo-driven, with no measured results, but the memory/reasoning-trace structure is a copyable pattern.

takeaways.technique: Reasoning-trace memory as a queryable store
takeaways.what_they_do: Persist the 'why' behind agent decisions (policies applied, risk factors, prior decisions) as structured records tied to entities, so future runs retrieve prior decision provenance instead of only the final output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: reasoning traces give us the ability to understand why decisions were made and how they're done

takeaways.technique: Graph/relational retrieval over pure vector similarity
takeaways.what_they_do: Combine vector lookup with relationship traversal so retrieval returns the connected history (prior diagnosis, prior operations) rather than just semantically similar chunks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there is certain things which are background information that was lost in the similarity search

takeaways.technique: Feedback loop: agent output written back into shared memory
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent loop pushes results back into context memory, and subsequent queries pull them back as reasoning traces, making the store self-reinforcing across tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's then pushing that back into the context memory which gets added back into the graph

takeaways.what_they_do: Expose the exact nodes/edges used to reach a decision so a human can audit and justify it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this is why knowledge graphs make things explainable and auditable because now we see exactly the information which is being populated
